THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, MONDAY, JUNE 30, 1924.
（批：8645 30/6/24.）

THE KU KLUX KLAN
As It Was in Its Origination:
Recent Revival an Off-Shoot
of Blonde Beast Idea

BY GEORGE E. SOKOLSKY.

In the United States, the original Ku Klux Klan came into existence as a result of the Civil War. Negroes only just freed from economic and political slavery, rough and unrighteous northerners known as carpet-baggers, coming into the south to make what they could out of the misfortunes of a fine people defeated in war, banded together. The young men of the south had to find means of defending their moral and social rights, their homes and women folk, from such a combination. They eventually organized the Klan, the night-riders of which garbed in flowing white robes, hooded, silent, bearing a Fiery Cross, acted as a police force for the enforcement of moral law in the chaotic south. Such bodies appear everywhere in the world in similar circumstances. Such bodies have appeared in China in the form of volunteer organization.

In due course, the Klan disappears from American history. Like similar institutions, when the immediate cause for its organization disappeared, the better element retired, disintegration and dishonesty set in and the movement went to pieces. Some years ago, Thomas Dixon, an American author, wrote a novel on the subject which David Griffith arranged for the screen in the form of "The Birth of a Nation." The picture is perhaps one of the only true screen classics, for it has been showing for many years and the public seems never to tire of it. It has very patently influenced American public opinion, has recrystallized the anti-negro feeling) and has given a background in romance for a peculiar racial movement developing in the United States simultaneously with the nationalistic unmeasured chauvinism attending the War.

The Fair Hair Fallacy.

This movement might go by the name of the Superiority of the Nordics. It will be remembered that the Germans had for many decades preached the superiority of the Teutons over all human beings. The blonde beast of Nietzsche was ridiculed during the clamour of the war, but the idea sunk into the minds of many non-Germans who were themselves blonde, blue-eyed, tall and of apparent Teutonic origin. Houston Stewart Chamberlain, a Briton born, but a German by citizenship and affinity, son-in-law of Wagner, a follower of Thor and Parsifal, a wearer of an Iron Cross and the most abject of scholarly panderers to the Kaiser, wrote two fat and wearisome volumes called, "The Foundations of the 20th Century," in which he tried to prove that everything good and valuable in the civilization of the human race was of Aryan, Teutonic origin. He forgets the achievements of the Huns, the Ephthalites, the Turks and other peoples of Mongolia and Central Asia, the mixture of peoples in the Mediterranean, of Asiatic, African, European and Indo-European. What is good was done by someone with blonde or red hair or by one who should have blonde or red hair. He even claims that Jesus Christ was a Teuton because all pictures of Him show blonde hair!

This idea of the superiority of the blondeness fitted well with social conditions in the United States. For there, although the country is republican, a social aristocracy of Anglo-Saxons has developed over the large mass of mixed nationality. The names of the holders of high public office indicate the significance of this Anglo-Saxon aristocracy: Lincoln, Johnson, Buchanan, Arthur, Garfield, Roosevelt, McKinley, Cleveland, Wilson, Harding, Coolidge—not a Slavic, Latin, or Semitic name anywhere. The pure Anglo-Saxon or Scotch-Irish Protestant class in the United States has remained predominant throughout American history and is likely to remain such, for with restricted immigration, the numerical attack on this class is weakened.

The Nordic Theory.

Certain pseudo-scientists utilized the German idea of the superiority of the Teuton, changed the word Teuton to Nordic, got enthusiastic about Scandinavia and launched an attack on the civilization of everything which was not Teutonic in origin.

Into the rights and wrongs of the theory behind such a movement, it is impossible to go here. The fact of the movement is sufficient. It was widespread and general. It led to adhesion of similarly-minded people who sought to preserve the type of politics and social institution which they knew and liked to live under. It led to a distrust of the alien in the United States, particularly the Southern and Eastern European, the Semite and the Asiatic. The fact that radicalism in the United States was as much a political tendency among the New England old families such as the Lowells, the Longfellows and the Danas, did not seem to disturb the general opinion that all radical, and therefore un-American movements were organized, financed and strengthened by adhesions from eastern and southern Europe.

Henry Ford's Mistake.

Henry Ford was a strong element in this movement. It is no secret that the master tinker was led into his most startling absurdity by a Jewish woman from Vienna, Rozika Schwimmer. This lady got Ford to organize the peace expedition. She made the arrangements. He was the goat. Ford's bitterness toward Rozika, his shame at being ridiculed, his loss of face, were not to be forgotten. Like other men at other times, he took it out of the Jews. Using the old Russian monarchical organization and allying himself with the Tory "Morning Post" which was also associated with Russian monarchism, he started a world-wide campaign to extirpate the Jew.

All Things to All Haters.

All these forces working together, from different angles, made possible that curious tendency in American political and social life, the Ku Klux Klan. This organization adopted the paraphernalia of a historic movement, hallowed in the minds of many fine people in the United States; it adopted the historical point of view of the Anglo-Saxon aristocracy in the United States, of the socially best people; it supported itself with the natural antipathy to people of alien habits and civilization. It utilized the fear in the United States for the radicalism of Russia, the dread of negro infiltrations and of Asiatic immigration. It adopted the creed that the United States must remain White and Protestant, that moral law must be upheld by popular force as the written law is by political force and that the non-white, non-Protestant elements in the United States must be held in their "proper" place, the propriety of their place to be determined by the individual Klan of each locality.

When the Klan first reappeared it was principally engaged in anti-negro and anti-radical activity. In due course, however, it became a sort of fomentor of hatreds. Where the Jews were unpopular, it was anti-Semitic; where the Catholics were disliked, it was anti-Catholic; where the negro was disliked, it was anti-negro. It was all things to all haters. Its platform was hatred. It appealed to the spirit of the Druids. The "New York World" was the first American newspaper to investigate and in a measure to destroy the glamour of the Klan. It soon found that the Klan was a business organization, engaged in selling night-gowns and hoods, in publishing literature and in getting members. It found that certain individuals, particularly the Imperial Wizard, were making a fortune out of the business and that professional press-agents and similar exploiters of public opinion were engaged at high salaries to put the Klan over. Henceforth, good people were not connected with the Klan. It began to disintegrate. The Imperial Wizard was made to resign. Faction fights entered the Klan. Nevertheless the organization is not yet dead, as the appearance of it as a political force at the Democratic Convention indicates.

三K党
其起源时的面貌：
近期的复兴是“金发野兽”思想的分支

作者：乔治·E·索科尔斯基 (GEORGE E. SOKOLSKY)。

在美国，最初的三K党是内战的结果而产生的。刚从经济和政治奴役中解放出来的黑人，以及被称为“提包客”(carpet-baggers)的粗鲁且不公正的北方人——他们来到南方，企图从一个在战争中战败的优秀民族的不幸中捞取利益——这些人纠集在一起。南方的年轻人不得不寻找手段，以保护他们的道德和社会权利、家园以及女性亲属，免受这种组合的侵害。他们最终组织了三K党，其夜间骑手身披飘逸的白色长袍，头戴兜帽，沉默无声，手持火焰十字架，在混乱的南方充当执行道德法律的警察力量。在世界各地的类似情况下，此类团体都会出现。此类团体也以志愿组织的形式出现在中国。

适时地，三K党从美国历史上消失了。像类似的机构一样，当其组织的直接原因消失后，较好的分子退出，瓦解和欺诈随之产生，运动分崩离析。几年前，美国作家托马斯·迪克森 (Thomas Dixon) 就此主题写了一部小说，大卫·格里菲斯 (David Griffith) 将其改编为电影《一个国家的诞生》(The Birth of a Nation)。这部影片或许是最真正的银幕经典之一，因为它已放映多年，而公众似乎从未厌倦。它非常明显地影响了美国舆论，使反黑人情绪重新结晶，并为一种特殊的种族运动提供了浪漫背景，该运动在美国的发展与伴随战争而来的民族主义无节制的沙文主义同时发生。

金发谬论。

这场运动可以称为“北欧人优越论”。人们会记得，德国人在几十年来一直宣扬条顿人优于所有人类。尼采的“金发野兽”在战争的喧嚣中受到嘲笑，但这一思想沉入了许多非德国人的脑海中，这些人本身也是金发、蓝眼、高大，且显然具有条顿血统。休斯顿·斯图尔特·张伯伦 (Houston Stewart Chamberlain) 生于英国，但入籍德国并与德国有亲和关系，他是瓦格纳的女婿，托尔 (Thor) 和帕西法尔 (Parsifal) 的追随者，铁十字勋章佩戴者，也是向凯撒献媚的最卑躬屈膝的学者之一，他写了两本厚重且令人厌倦的书，名为《十九世纪的基础》(The Foundations of the 19th Century，注：原文误作20世纪)，试图证明人类文明中一切美好和有价值的东西都源于雅利安人、条顿人。他忘记了匈奴人、嚈哒人、土耳其人以及其他蒙古和中亚民族的成就，忘记了地中海地区亚洲人、非洲人、欧洲人和印欧人的混合。凡是好的事物，都是由金发或红发的人，或者本该拥有金发或红发的人所做的。他甚至声称耶稣基督是条顿人，因为所有的画像都显示他是金发！

这种金发优越论的思想很好地适应了美国的社会状况。因为在那里，虽然国家是共和制的，但在大量混合国籍的人群之上，已经发展出一个盎格鲁-撒克逊人的社会贵族阶层。担任高级公职者的名字表明了这种盎格鲁-撒克逊贵族的重要性：林肯、约翰逊、布坎南、阿瑟、加菲尔德、罗斯福、麦金莱、克利夫兰、威尔逊、哈定、柯立芝——其中没有一个斯拉夫、拉丁或闪米特名字。美国的纯盎格鲁-撒克逊或苏格兰-爱尔兰新教徒阶级在整个美国历史上一直保持主导地位，并且可能会继续保持这种地位，因为随着移民限制，对该阶级的人数攻击被削弱了。

北欧理论。

某些伪科学家利用了德国关于条顿人优越性的思想，将“条顿”一词改为“北欧”，对斯堪的纳维亚半岛充满热情，并对一切非条顿起源的文明发起攻击。

在此不可能深入探讨支持此类运动的理论背后的对错。运动的事实本身就足够了。它是广泛且普遍的。它导致了志同道合者的加入，这些人试图保留他们所熟知并喜欢生活的政治和社会制度类型。它导致了对美国的外国人的不信任，特别是来自南欧和东欧的人、闪米特人和亚洲人。美国的激进主义同样是新英格兰老家族（如洛厄尔家族、朗费罗家族和达纳家族）中的一种政治倾向，这一事实似乎并没有扰乱普遍的看法，即所有激进的、因此是非美国的运动都是由来自东欧和南欧的依附者组织、资助和加强的。

亨利·福特的错误。

亨利·福特是这场运动中的一个重要因素。众所周知，这位大师级工匠被一位来自维也纳的犹太女性罗齐卡·施维默 (Rozika Schwimmer) 引入了他最惊人的荒谬之中。这位女士让福特组织了和平远征队。她做了安排。他是替罪羊。福特对罗齐卡的怨恨、因被嘲笑而感到羞耻以及丢脸，都是无法忘记的。像其他时代的其他人一样，他将怒气发泄在犹太人身上。利用旧的俄罗斯君主制组织，并与同样与俄罗斯君主制有关的保守派《晨邮报》(Morning Post) 结盟，他发起了一场世界范围内的消灭犹太人的运动。

迎合所有仇恨者。

所有这些力量从不同角度共同作用，使得美国政治和社会生活中那种奇特的倾向——三K党——成为可能。该组织采用了一场历史运动的装备，这场运动在美国许多优秀人士的脑海中是神圣的；它采用了美国盎格鲁-撒克逊贵族、即社会上最优秀人士的历史观点；它依靠对外国习惯和文明的人的自然反感来支持自己。它利用了美国对俄罗斯激进主义的恐惧、对黑人渗透和亚洲移民的 dread（畏惧）。它采纳了这样一种信条：美国必须保持白人和新教特征，道德法律必须由民众力量来维护，正如成文法由政治力量维护一样，而美国境内的非白人、非新教分子必须被控制在他们的“适当”位置，其位置的适当性由每个地方的个别三K党分部决定。

当三K党首次重现时，它主要从事反黑人和反激进活动。然而，适时地，它变成了一种仇恨的煽动者。在犹太人不受欢迎的地方，它是反犹的；在天主教徒被厌恶的地方，它是反天主教的；在黑人不被喜欢的地方，它是反黑人的。它是所有仇恨者的万事通。它的纲领就是仇恨。它诉诸德鲁伊教的精神。《纽约世界报》(New York World) 是第一份调查并在一定程度上破坏三K党光环的美国报纸。它很快发现，三K党是一个商业组织，从事出售睡袍和兜帽、出版文献和招募成员的业务。它发现某些个人，特别是帝国巫师 (Imperial Wizard)，正从这项业务中发财，并且受聘高薪的专业新闻代理人和类似的舆论剥削者来推广三K党。从此以后，好人不再与三K党有关联。它开始瓦解。帝国巫师被迫辞职。派系斗争进入三K党。尽管如此，该组织尚未消亡，正如它在民主党全国代表大会上作为一股政治力量的出现所表明的那样。

that the Chinese Ku Klux Klan was
a Chinese organization, one jestel

save their country, yet it is not

foreign consulate for protection and

eigners and not Chinese. Had this
movement been given a chance to
develop and grow into something

Chinese. They do not claim to be

China. They are outsiders utilizing
the misfortunes of a nation to stir
up the unfortunate and to make
trouble for the miserable. For
such foreigners there can only be
one just punishment, a ship home-
ward bound.

Our Brothers.
As we are bound together for mutual benefits we must protect each others, namely:—give medical aid when sick, give relief when in poverty, in employment, in difficulties and bury the dead.

ORDER OF THE THREE K'S
Editor,
THE SHANGHAI TIMES
Sir,—In your article in THE
SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES of this
date you have made the usual
error that foreign papers like to
make, that is if any movement
is started it is blamed on the
students, etc. Now the Order
of the Three K's has no affilia-
tion with any student body or
movement. it is not political and
neither is it Bolshevik. It is a
movement of Chinese who like
to better their country and them-
selves without the aid of foreign
money or influence. So far all
the interests in Chinese affairs
of sport and education have
been started by foreign societies
usually having a religious affilia-
tion. This society is not re-
ligious.
The objects of the society as
mentioned are correct, and it is
true that we will take care of
a brother in case of sickness or
death and his family, surely you
will not object if the Chinese
try to help each other. As far
as any military leader using the
order for a mouthpiece, well, we
don't know about it if they do,
and we can assure you that it
will be far from the case. We
have no affiliations with any
military leaders, neither do we
desire to have such.
As to it being anti-foreign.
Why do all foreign papers make
that statement when any Chinese
society is started? It is not
anti-foreign and never will be.
We aim only to promote good
feeling between the Chinese and
the foreigners, but we certainly
have the right to organize our-
selves as well as the foreigner.
He has his secret societies like
the Masons, Odd Fellows and
hundreds of other secret socie-
ties, then why cannot the Chin-
ese have a society that is for the
Chinese and China?
Why cannot we agree to pur-
chase Chinese goods? Is there
any wrong in trying to boost our
own products?
The Chinese Ku Klux Klan is
not trying the impossible, but we
believe that we will be enabled
to better ourselves and perhaps
the country, not by killing or
threats, but by education and
assistance.
As to membership, perhaps
you are right and then again
perhaps you are wrong, but we
will say that you are a long way
under the estimate. Chinese are
not so much asleep as you per-
haps think.
Thanking you that you will
correct this impression of the
Three K's being a student move-
ment and anti-foreign,
We remain sincerely yours, for
the betterment of China and the
Chinese.
THE IMPERIAL KLAN
K.
Shanghai, May 18, 1924.

編輯，
《字林西報》
先生，—在您本日《字林西報星期日版》的文章中，
您犯了外國報紙喜歡犯的常見錯誤，即如果有任何運動
發起，就歸咎於學生等。現在，三K黨秩序
與任何學生團體或運動沒有關聯。它不是政治性的，
也不是布爾什維克。這是一場中國人希望改善他們的國家和他們
自身，而不依賴外國資金或影響的運動。迄今為止，所有涉及中國事務
的體育和教育興趣都是由通常具有宗教關聯的外國社團
發起的。本社團不具有宗教性質。
信中提到的社團目標是正確的，確實，我們會在兄弟生病或死亡時照顧他
和他的家人，當然，您不會反對中國人
試圖互相幫助。至於任何軍事領袖利用該
秩序作為傳聲筒，嗯，如果他們這樣做，我們也不知情，
我們可以向您保證，情況絕非如此。我們
與任何軍事領袖都沒有關聯，也不希望
有這樣的關聯。
至於它是反外國的。
為什麼每當中國社團成立時，所有外國報紙都做出
這樣的聲明？它不是反外國的，將來也不會是。
我們的目標只是促進中國人和外國人之間的友好
感情，但我們當然有權像外國人一樣組織
我們自己。他有他的秘密社團，如共濟會、獨立奇士會
和數百個其他秘密社團，那麼為什麼中國人
不能有一個為中國人和中國服務的社團呢？
為什麼我們不能同意購買國貨？試圖推廣我們自己的產品有什麼錯嗎？
中國三K黨並沒有嘗試不可能的事情，但我們相信，我們將能夠改善我們自身，也許還能改善國家，不是通過殺戮或威脅，而是通過教育和援助。
至於成員數量，也許您是對的，也許您是錯的，但我們要說，您的估計遠遠偏低。中國人並不像您可能認為的那樣沉睡。
感謝您糾正三K黨是學生運動和反外國的這種印象，
為了中國和中國人的福祉，
我們誠摯地屬於您，
帝國三K黨
K.
上海，1924年5月18日。

THE CHINESE KU
KLUX KLAN

There has been a good deal of scepticism as to the statement made in the columns of these papers that a Chinese Ku Klux Klan had been formed and that the membership ran into several thousands. In THE SUNDAY TIMES we made detailed reference to certain documents that had come into our possession, and these revealed the objects of "The Three K's." If any doubt remained in the minds of readers after the publication of that article, it is unlikely that they will be convinced by the letter which we publish in our correspondence column this morning. Having some months ago met at least one member of the Klan in Shanghai, and having made elaborate inquiries since receipt of the documents referred to on Sunday, we have no doubt as to the existence in Shanghai, Canton, Hangchow, Nanking and Hankow of the Ku Klux Klan, the principal aim of which, as we have said, is the maintenance of the republican form of Government in China, and to combat all forces detrimental to the maintenance of such a government. "The Imperial Klan" to-day takes us to task for suggesting the possibility that this is a student movement, and says that "The Order of the Three K's" has "no affiliation with any student body or movement, it is not political and neither is it Bolshevik." We did not say any of these things, but wrote that one of the documents before us pointed out that "few of the students who have participated in any of the student movements, and have imbibed the principles of student patriotic endeavour, should resist the appeal." Neither did we suggest that the Klan was connected with, for instance, that secret society that has obtained a grip on Chinese all along the Yangtze Valley, and the name of which is mentioned only in a whisper by non-members.

"The Imperial Klan" states that the Klan movement in China is that of Chinese who like to better their country and themselves without the aid of foreign money or influence. This, obviously, is most laudable, whatever we may think of the possibilities of China evolving order out of the present chaos, brought about by rapacious officials, military satraps and men whose political jealousies have over-ridden commonsense. Even the Klan acknowledges that the foreigner has done some good in China, and if they desire only to improve upon what the alien has done in their midst and to benefit by the mistakes that have been made in the past, then we wish them every possible success. But, in moving along lines of isolation from the foreigner, there must always be a danger of becoming antagonistic, and the safer plan surely would be to do all that is in their power to better their country without stating any exceptions as to assistance. In that event it would be impossible for anyone to suspect that the movement was anti-foreign, or, what is more important, for members to act as if it were. We are glad to learn that any such suspicions of anti-foreign motives are incorrect and that the Klan will never be anti-foreign as it is aimed "to promote good feeling between the Chinese and the foreigners."

Why there should constantly be discussion revealing prejudice against the foreigner we fail to see, although no doubt it owes genesis lay in the antagonism always displayed by China to aliens and their works. There is no suggestion in England of hostility to the Chinese or any other nationality, although there are some who are unable, as yet, to enjoy the company or relations in business of those nationals who were their enemies in the later war. But, then, every man is not congenial to every other man. Racial antipathies arising from war are, however, usually healed by the greatest physician of all—time. No sensible foreigner can object to the Chinese trying to supply their own needs: it is one of the aims of Western nations so far as practicable, to make themselves self-supporting. This policy was emphasized in the Great War, when it was extremely hazardous to traffic overseas. China undoubtedly could supply as many of her own needs as any Power, but the day when she will do so is far off, and its dawn will not take place earlier by China neglecting to accept the experience and practical aid of those who have passed through the undeveloped stage to high efficiency. We are assured that the Klan is not attempting the impossible, and that they are seeking to better themselves and the country by education and assistance. In that event there need be no alarm at the strength of the Klan: that is so long as their methods are in accord with their principles.

中国三K党

对于本报栏目中关于已成立中国三K党且会员人数达数千人的说法，存在不少怀疑。在《星期泰晤士报》中，我们详细提及了某些已落入我们手中的文件，这些文件揭示了“三K党”的目标。如果读者在发表那篇文章后心中仍存疑虑，他们不太可能因我们今天在来信专栏刊登的这封信而被说服。几个月前，我们在上海至少见过一名该党成员，并且在收到周日提到的文件后进行了详尽的调查，因此我们毫不怀疑三K党在上海、广州、杭州、南京和汉口的存在，其主要目标，正如我们所说，是维护中国的共和政体，并对抗一切不利于维持这种政体的力量。“帝国党”今天指责我们暗示这可能是一场学生运动，并称“三K党”“与任何学生团体或运动均无关联，它不是政治性的，也不是布尔什维克式的”。我们并未说过这些话，而是写道，我们面前的一份文件指出，“那些参与了任何学生运动并吸收了学生爱国奋斗原则的学生，很少会拒绝这一号召”。我们也未暗示三K党与例如那个在整个长江流域控制了中国人的秘密社团有关联，非成员提到其名时也只是低声耳语。

“帝国党”称，中国的三K党运动是由那些希望在没有外国资金或影响援助的情况下改善其国家和自身的中国人发起的。无论我们对从中国目前由贪婪官员、军阀政客以及政治嫉妒心压倒常识的人所造成的混乱中演变出秩序的可能性持何种看法，这显然是最值得称赞的。甚至三K党也承认外国人在中国做了一些好事，如果他们只是希望改进外人在他们中间所做的工作，并从过去所犯的错误中受益，那么我们祝愿他们取得尽可能大的成功。但是，在沿着与外国人隔离的路线前进时，总是存在变得敌对的风险，更安全的计划无疑是在不声明任何援助例外的情况下，尽其所能改善他们的国家。在这种情况下，任何人都不可能怀疑该运动是排外的，或者更重要的是，成员们表现得好像它是排外的一样。我们很高兴获悉，任何关于排外动机的怀疑都是不正确的，并且三K党永远不会排外，因为其目标是“促进中外之间的友好感情”。

为何会不断出现揭示出对外国人偏见的讨论，我们看不出来，尽管毫无疑问，其根源在于中国对外国人及其作品一贯表现出的敌意。在英国，并没有针对中国人或任何其他国籍的敌意建议，尽管有些人尚无法享受那些在后期战争中曾是他们的敌人的国民的陪伴或商业关系。但是，毕竟不是每个人都彼此投缘。然而，由战争引起的种族反感通常会被最伟大的医生——时间——所治愈。理智的外国人不会反对中国人尝试满足自身需求：这是西方国家在可行范围内使自身自给自足的目标之一。这一政策在大战期间得到了强调，当时海外贸易极其危险。中国无疑能像任何强国一样满足自身的许多需求，但她做到这一点的那一天还遥遥无期，而如果中国忽视接受那些已从欠发达阶段走向高效阶段的人的经验和实际援助，其黎明就不会更早到来。我们确信，三K党并未尝试不可能之事，他们正寻求通过教育和援助来改善自身和国家。如果是这样，就不必对三K党的实力感到恐慌：只要他们的方法符合其原则即可。

CHINESE KU KLUX KLAN
IN SHANGHAI

A STUDENT MOVEMENT?

Organization Revealed In Documents
Distributed Among Natives

Has the Ku Klux Klan, that infamous American order of masked justice, come to China? That is a question affecting public safety which arises from an examination of some remarkable documents which have come into the possession of THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES. These documents, copies of which have been distributed to likely members, refer to the formation of an organization of the "Order of the Three K's," under "The Imperial Klan." The authenticity of the movement is worthy of consideration because our informant states: "There is no question but that the Chinese are, at present, ready for such a movement, and it would be a big source of anti-foreign spirit. This, I believe, is the object of the order."

Patriotism Behind It

The driving force of this new organization, judging from the documents, which include an invitation to join and a statement of the aims, is some degree of patriotism. Whether its activities will emulate those of the American order, whose acts of barbarism perpetrated under the mask of intense patriotism have earned for the organization world-wide abhorrence, remain to be seen. Yet, it cannot be denied that such a movement is possible of introduction in China, where secret societies and "paungs" have been known for centuries.

A large strata of Chinese society, that strata which produces the criminal element, is honeycombed with secret orders. The loafers have their society; the robbers have their society. Whole towns and provinces have societies or "paungs," strange orders demanding undying loyalty to principles and ideas unknown to foreigners. The only conclusion that can be attached to the new order is that it is purely a student body, perhaps arising from ideas transmitted from America through returned students, or built on the sensational stories of Ku Klux Klan activities which form an important part of the breakfast tidings in the newspapers. The dire penalties for infringement of Klan secrets, however, may be ignored if it is a student body.

Six months ago a story was published in this paper announcing the formation of a Chinese Ku Klux Klan. It was stated that even the white gown and hood, the impressive vestment of this strange form of hooded justice, had been adopted, a yellow dragon replacing the scarlet cross of the American Klan. The objects were stated to be war on the many abuses gnawing the fabric of government in China, corruption, peculation, dishonesty among the politicians, "squeezes" and the struggle for power at the cost of national integrity.

The Klan documents in our possession confirm what was previously written. These are the objects of the Klan: Our country, right or wrong; Our brothers; Our family; Education; Industry. "Give us your answer as soon as possible so we may grasp you by the hand in the grip of brotherhood and help to preserve our country as a nation among the great Powers of the world" is the appeal to prospective members, as stated on the membership form.

5 Klans; 10,000 Members

According to our information, five Klans have been formed—at Canton, Shanghai, Hangchow, Nanking and Hankow—all of which places are centres of student activity. In and around Shanghai it is understood that there are 10,000 members. The members are elected in this way: the name of a likely member is submitted to the principals of the order, and after his status has been carefully investigated, and his opinions and principles, as known to friends in the order, have been considered, he is invited to join the Klan. After he has been given time to consider the proposal a Klansman calls on him for his answer, and if he is agreeable his name is inscribed on the roll.

Few of the students who have participated in any of the student movements, and have imbibed the principles of student patriotic endeavour, should resist the appeal: "We are glad to have you in our ranks, and we know you can play an active part in this potential force to help our country."

"The Three K's"

The creed of the Klan is outlined in a document headed "Objects of the Three K's." The Klan believes in a Republican form of government and the maintenance of such a government constitutes their principal aim, as well as war on all forces detrimental to the maintenance of such a government. Monarchy is alien to the Klan.

The Klan supports and encourages education and supports the building of more schools so that the Chinese schools "can grow as efficiently and throughout the land." Purchase freely as the green grass grows of Chinese-made goods, patronage of shops selling Chinese-made goods, and support of Chinese industries are also among the Klan's objects.

Family Reverence

A strange spirit of family reverence runs throughout the document: "As we are banded together for mutual benefit we must protect our brothers, provide medical aid in case of sickness, give succour when in poverty or unemployment, or other difficulties, and to arrange for proper burial for the dead. Mother, wife and children are very dear to us and we must, therefore, give comfort and shelter to them and shield them from harm."

These are the facts of this new organization. Whether it will ever prove effective depends on the seriousness with which its members take up the work. One thing is certain: the organization is not likely to grow to the extent of the American Klan, for will its history be written in so many chapters of lawlessness and cold-blooded murder as in some of the Southern States of America. One wonders, however, whether it is not one of these schemes hatched up by politicians to have a loud and noisy following of students in the next struggle for dominance when President Tsao Kun has been shuffled out of the Presidency!

在上海

是一场学生运动吗？

在分发给本地人的文件中披露的组织

那个臭名昭著的美国蒙面正义组织“三K党”来到中国了吗？这是《上海星期时报》获得的一些非凡文件所引发的一个关乎公共安全的问题。这些文件的副本已分发给可能的成员，其中提到了在“帝国三K党”之下组建一个“三个K字秩序会”（Order of the Three K's）的组织。该运动的真实性值得考量，因为我们的线人声称：“毫无疑问，中国人目前正准备进行这样的运动，而这将成为反外情绪的一大源头。我相信，这就是该秩序会的目的。”

其背后的爱国主义

从包括入会邀请和宗旨陈述在内的文件来看，这一新组织的驱动力是某种程度的爱国主义。它的活动是否会效仿美国那个组织——后者以强烈的爱国主义为面具实施野蛮行径，从而招致全世界的憎恶——仍有待观察。然而，不可否认的是，这种运动有可能被引入中国，因为秘密会社和“帮”（paungs）在这里已存在了数个世纪。

中国社会的一个庞大阶层，即产生犯罪分子的阶层，遍布着各种秘密秩序。游手好闲者有他们的会社；强盗有他们的会社。整个城镇和省份都有会社或“帮”，这些奇怪的秩序要求成员对外国人所不知的原则和理念保持至死不渝的忠诚。对于这个新秩序，唯一能得出的结论是，它纯粹是一个学生团体，或许源于归国留学生从美国传来的思想，或者是建立在报纸早餐新闻中占据重要地位的、关于三K党活动的耸人听闻的故事之上。不过，如果这确实是一个学生团体，那么违反三K党秘密所面临的严厉惩罚可能会被忽视。

六个月前，本报刊登了一则消息，宣布中国三K党成立。据报道，甚至连白袍和头罩——这种奇特的蒙面正义形式令人印象深刻的服饰——也被采用，只是用一条黄龙取代了美国三K党的红色十字。据称，其目标是向侵蚀中国政府结构的诸多弊病开战，包括腐败、贪污、政客中的不诚实行为、“勒索”（squeezes）以及以牺牲国家完整为代价的权力斗争。

我们手中的三K党文件证实了此前报道的内容。以下是三K党的宗旨：我们的国家，无论对错；我们的兄弟；我们的家庭；教育；工业。入会申请表上写道：“请尽快给予答复，以便我们在兄弟情谊的紧握中与你携手，帮助我们的国家作为世界列强中的一员得以保全。”这是对潜在成员的呼吁。

5个三K党分部；10,000名成员

根据我们所获信息，已在广州、上海、杭州、南京和汉口成立了五个三K党分部，这些地方都是学生活动的中心。据悉，在上海及其周边地区有10,000名成员。成员的选举方式如下：将潜在成员的姓名提交给该秩序会的首领，在仔细调查其身份，并考虑其在秩序会内的朋友所了解的其观点和原则后，邀请其加入三K党。给予其时间考虑该提议后，一名三K党员会登门征求其答复，如果其同意，则将其名字登记在册。

那些参与过任何学生运动并吸收了学生爱国奋斗原则的学生，很少会拒绝这样的呼吁：“我们很高兴你加入我们的行列，我们知道你能在这股潜在的力量中发挥积极作用，以帮助我们的国家。”

“三个K字”

三K党的信条在一份题为“三个K字之宗旨”的文件中概述。三K党信奉共和政体，维护此类政府构成其主要目标，同时也向所有不利于维护此类政府的力量开战。君主制与三K党格格不入。

三K党支持并鼓励教育，支持建设更多的学校，以便中国学校“能够高效地在全国范围内发展”。像青草生长一样自由购买国货，光顾出售国货的商店，以及支持中国工业，也是三K党的目标之一。

家族尊崇

文件中贯穿着一种奇特的家族尊崇精神：“既然我们为了共同利益而结盟，我们就必须保护我们的兄弟，在生病时提供医疗援助，在贫困、失业或其他困难时给予救济，并为死者安排适当的葬礼。母亲、妻子和子女对我们来说非常珍贵，因此，我们必须给予他们安慰和庇护，并保护他们免受伤害。”

以上就是这个新组织的事实。它是否会被证明有效，取决于其成员对待工作的认真程度。有一点是肯定的：该组织不太可能发展到美国三K党那样的规模，因为它的历史不会像在美国南部一些州那样，写满无法无天和冷血谋杀的篇章。然而，人们不禁怀疑，这是否是政客们策划的方案之一，旨在曹锟总统被赶下台后的下一次权力争夺中，拥有一群大声喧哗的学生追随者！

THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, SEPTEMBER 2, 1923.

KU KLUX KLAN
IN SHANGHAI

STUDENTS GET BUSY

White-Hood Organization
Comes To China

WHAT WILL THEY DO?

The Chinese Ku Klux Klan,
which will carry on activities
similar to the American organiza-
tion, is the latest aberration of
a number of Chinese students in
Shanghai, according to a report
received by the SUNDAY TIMES
yesterday.
Returned students from Ame-
rica brought the intimate de-
tails of the organization with
them, and the Chinese version
of the white hooded horde is to
be based on the parent
organization. Already a large
number of students are reported
to have sworn their allegiance
to the new body. In addition to
Shanghai, a branch at Nanking,
and another in Peking are in
the process of formation so that
the whole nation will feel the
effect of the powerful associa-
tion—that is, if it ever gets be-
yond the stage of a mere farce
—a very doubtful speculation.

A Tremendous Oath

The Klan trappings, so im-
pressive and majestic in the flash-
light pictures of Klan gather-
ings occasionally given in pri-
vileged papers, have not been
neglected. A white gown and
hood, not bordered with a red
cross, but with a red or yellow
dragon, according to the many
degrees which will distinguish
the Klansmen, will be worn. A
solemn and tremendous oath,
consecrating members to the
service of the country and
eradication of abuses in the
secret and drastic manner of
the Klan, will be administered
to all members
Naturally, the proceedings
will be in secret, and the utmost
secrecy will be observed in all
its workings, but the informa-
tion gives the impression that
such secrecy will not exist for
long. What will undoubtedly
happen will be that the Klan
will be nothing but one of the
noisy protestant student or-
ganizations with which every-
body in China is familiar. Such
important pieces of statecraft
as bombarding ministers with
telegrams, manifestos, appeals,
memoranda and the like, and
strikes at schools when one
student objects to his teacher,
will doubtless be all they will
accomplish.
The Chinese students have
Stetson hats, American shoes,
and an American twang about
their English so perhaps in
their desire to emulate Ameri-
cans they had to establish the
Ku Klux Klan.

《上海星期时报》，1923年9月2日。

三K党
在上海

学生们忙起来了

戴白头罩的组织
来到中国

他们会做什么？

据《星期时报》昨日收到的一份报告称，中国三K党将在上海开展与美国组织类似的活动，这是上海部分中国学生的最新怪异举动。

从美国归来的留学生带回了该组织的详细内幕，而这个戴白头罩的中国版群体将以美国母组织为基础。据报道，已有大量学生宣誓效忠这个新团体。除了上海，南京和北京的分部也在组建过程中，以便让整个国家感受到这个强大协会的影响——当然，前提是它能超越仅仅是一场闹剧的阶段，这是一个非常值得怀疑的推测。

庄严的誓言

三K党的装束，即在偶尔见于特权报刊的三K党集会闪光灯照片中显得令人印象深刻且威严的那些，并未被忽视。成员将穿着白袍和头罩，边缘不是饰以红十字，而是根据区分不同等级三K党员的许多级别，饰以红龙或黄龙。所有成员都将接受一项庄严而巨大的誓言，以三K党秘密且严厉的方式，奉献成员服务于国家并根除弊病。

自然，活动过程将是秘密的，其所有运作都将严守最高机密，但所获信息给人的印象是，这种秘密状态不会持续太久。毫无疑问将会发生的情况是，三K党只不过会成为中国人人都熟悉的那种喧闹的学生抗议组织之一。诸如用电报、宣言、呼吁书、备忘录等轰炸部长们，以及当一名学生对老师不满时在学校举行罢工等重要的治国方略，无疑将是他们所能完成的全部事情。

中国学生戴着斯泰森帽（Stetson hats），穿着美国鞋，讲英语带着美国口音，所以也许在他们渴望模仿美国人的过程中，不得不建立三K党。

I. O. REQ

FILIPINO "K. K. K." IN REVOLT
FOR MANY YEARS

KATIPUNAN MORE ACTIVE

Members Required To Sign Own Name In
Blood; Centuries Of Atrocities

A Reuter's message published yesterday stated that Governor-General Wood is in favour of tact, discretion and tolerance in dealing with the turbulent elements in the Philippine Islands. The Katipunan Society, or League, that has figured in the recent despatches from Manila in connection with revolutionary activities of the Filipinos, is an ancient order that has played a prominent part in revolutions in the Philippines since 1872. Thousands of acts of atrocity are laid at its door. No power has ever been able to crush it. It is the K. K. K. of the Philippines, appearing in various forms since the treaty with Magellan was sealed in 1521 by the blood compact, or the Pacto de Sangre, memorialized in a painting by the Filipino artist, Juan Luna, which, for many years, had a prominent place on the walls of the Government palace in Manila, until finally removed by the Spanish after the revolution of 1896.

First introduced by the Chinese as an offshoot of the secret societies of that country, it adapted itself to the service of the Malay in his resistance to the various orders of the Spanish branch of the Roman Catholic Church in the Philippines. Today it primarily is political, but has all the traditions of a blood-thirsty past, when it wreaked its vengeance on the clerical orders which oppressed the native curé's equal station and prerogatives with the Spanish friar, wrung by oppressive fees and taxes the best of the crops and most of the earnings of the Filipinos, and bound them in service and enslaved them to cultivate the land, build monasteries and become menials of the lowest order. Realizing that only through superstition and the use of their spiritual authority could they hold the natives, they kept them in ignorance of all else. They organized themselves into corporations, secured great grant of the most valuable lands and amassed great wealth.

After its "suppression," through torture and persecution, in 1872, the Katipunan grew in strength and resolved itself into a spurious Masonic form, sworn "to remove by blood the bondage of Spain." The order took the name of Walanghang Katipunan ng mga Anak ng Bayan (Infinite Association of the Children of the Nation). It had numerous and scattered lodges. The officers still were the "Capitan," the "Punong," as well as the "Magdalo" and "Magdiwang" councils. All members signed the "Pacto de Sangre," or blood compact, which required the signature of a member in his own blood, drawn by a bolothrust in his breast.

Aguinaldo Kept Hatred Alive

Following the revolution of 1896 against Spain, the order was recruited and revivified by Andres Bonifacio, a schoolmaster of Cavite, a small town across the bay from Manila. It was in Bonifacio's school that Aguinaldo learned the rudiments of his education and through him was initiated into the secrets of the Katipunan. It was a powerful factor in the Filipino revolution of 1899-1900, and Bonifacio turned it into a war machine of the revolutionists against the Americans when the break came at the end of 1896. In his "palace" at Malolos Aguinaldo had ranged along the wall of his large reception room a dozen exhibits of Katipunan victims. These were effigies carved in wood, showing the various tortures executed by the priests and Spanish officials on the victims of Katipunan members or their families to extort the secrets of the order. They were mounted on bamboo pedestals and were painted so as to bring out all the gruesomeness of the blood-wringing brutalities practiced. By such devices was the hatred of the Malay kept alive and vengeful. They served admirably for recruiting propaganda.

In 1899 the Katipunan was turned into a part of the war machine to contest our sovereignty of the islands. The Sandatan branch—the bolo men—were quite effective in various parts of the islands, especially in terrorizing the natives into joining the revolution or preventing them from allying themselves with the Americans. The cochero or stableman was a secret Katipunan. The muchacho, or servant, secretly awaited the order to turn incendiary and was always a spy. In the office of the Governor General, in the surgical ward of the American hospital, in the kitchen of the commissary, in the telegraph office, at the mess table in camp—everywhere—was the Katipunan informer, whose bolo was hidden near by, whose quick ear was ever ready to "carry" the orders of the officer, and whose eyes were alert to observe actions that revealed projected movements of the troops.

菲律宾“K. K. K.”多年叛乱

卡蒂普南更为活跃

成员需用自身鲜血签名；数个世纪的暴行

昨日发表的一则路透社消息称，总督伍德（Wood）主张在处理菲律宾群岛的动荡分子时采取策略、谨慎和宽容的态度。近期来自马尼拉的急电中提及与菲律宾人革命活动有关的卡蒂普南社（Katipunan Society），或称联盟，是一个古老的组织，自1872年以来在菲律宾的革命中发挥了重要作用。数千起暴行被归咎于该组织。没有任何力量能够将其摧毁。它是菲律宾的 K. K. K.，自1521年麦哲伦条约通过血盟（Pacto de Sangre）缔结以来，以各种形式出现，这一事件被菲律宾艺术家胡安·卢纳（Juan Luna）的一幅画作所纪念，该画多年来一直悬挂在马尼拉政府宫殿的墙壁显眼处，直到1896年革命后最终被西班牙人移除。

它最初由中国人作为该国秘密会社的分支引入，随后适应马来人的需求，服务于其抵抗罗马天主教会在菲律宾的西班牙分支的各种修会。如今，它主要具有政治性质，但保留了嗜血过去的所有传统，当时它对那些压迫本地神父、使其地位与特权等同于西班牙修士的神职人员实施报复，通过苛捐杂税榨取菲律宾人最好的收成和大部分收入，并束缚他们服役，奴役他们耕种土地、建造修道院并成为最低等的仆役。他们意识到只有依靠迷信和利用其精神权威才能控制当地人，因此使当地人对其他一切事物保持无知。他们将自己组织成公司团体，获得了最宝贵土地的大量赠予，并积累了巨额财富。

在1872年通过酷刑和迫害对其进行“镇压”之后，卡蒂普南势力增强，并转变为一种伪共济会形式，宣誓“以鲜血解除西班牙的束缚”。该组织取名为 Walanghang Katipunan ng mga Anak ng Bayan（国民之子无限协会）。它拥有众多且分散的分会。官员仍然是“Capitan”、“Punong”，以及“Magdalo”和“Magdiwang”议会。所有成员都签署“Pacto de Sangre”，即血盟，这要求成员用刺入胸部的 bolo（大刀）流出的自身鲜血进行签名。

阿吉纳尔多保持仇恨活力

继1896年反对西班牙的革命之后，该组织由安德烈斯·博尼法西奥（Andres Bonifacio）招募并复兴，他是甲米地（Cavite）的一名校长，甲米地是马尼拉湾对面的一个小镇。阿吉纳尔多正是在博尼法西奥的学校里学习了基础教育的基础知识，并通过他加入了卡蒂普南的秘密。它是1899-1900年菲律宾革命中的一股强大力量，当1896年底关系破裂时，博尼法西奥将其转变为革命者对抗美国人的战争机器。在马洛洛斯（Malolos）的“宫殿”里，阿吉纳尔多在其大型接待室的墙上排列了十几件卡蒂普南受害者的展品。这些是用木头雕刻的人像，展示了牧师和西班牙官员对卡蒂普南成员或其家属的受害者施加的各种酷刑，以逼供该组织的秘密。它们被安装在竹制底座上，并经过彩绘，以突显那些榨取鲜血的残暴行为的恐怖程度。通过此类手段，马来人的仇恨得以保持鲜活并充满复仇情绪。它们极好地服务于招募宣传。

1899年，卡蒂普南转变为战争机器的一部分，以争夺我们对岛屿的主权。Sandatan 分支——即 bolo 刀手——在岛屿的各个地区相当有效，特别是在恐吓当地人加入革命或阻止他们与美国人结盟方面。马车夫或马夫是秘密的卡蒂普南成员。男仆或仆人秘密等待纵火的命令，并且始终是间谍。在总督办公室、美国医院的外科病房、军需处的厨房、电报局、营地的餐桌旁——无处不在——都有卡蒂普南的线人，他们的 bolo 刀藏在附近，敏锐的耳朵随时准备“传递”军官的命令，他们的眼睛警觉地观察着透露部队预定行动的动作。

During the campaign of 1899-
1900 our forces seldom "surpris-
ed" the Filipino army. They
always were ready to fight or
run. The secret Katipunan knew
all. In the guise of a farmer
returning through the lines, after
disposing of his produce, that
humble member of the wide-
stretching order carried the news
to his compatriot in the field;
whispered into his ear by a
jargon strange to the American
sentinel. The industrious fisher-
man, passing to and fro from
Laguna de Bay to Manila, up
and down the Pasig River, was
the messenger of the Katipunan.
He was watched. He was suspect-
ed, but seldom caught, and if
caught he pleaded amego—a
friend of the great and good
American—and, being humani-
tarians and big brothers, we be-
lieved him. But at night in the
windowless depths of a "go-
down"—warehouse—or in a
shamble in the Tondo, or native
section, he would glide in, bare-
footed and as stealthy as a cat,
and, by the light of a dip, hold
council, and gloat.

Secret Assemblies

Back of the Tondo Cathedral,
in the amego quarter, where all
the natives were Americanists,
"having been converted to
pacification," was a typical
assemblage place of the order.
A native of the Tagalog-hating
Province of Macabebe, acting
as an American spy, joined the
order and gained admittance to
the council in 1889. Into this
blackhole, the night of its dis-
covery and capture, had crept a
score of Katipunans, sworn by
the blood compact. Present was
the local chief of the Sandatahans,
orb bolo men, a man of
intelligence and cunning, daily
seen in his white duck
as head waiter at the lead-
ing hotel of the city, where many
officers and their families lived.
The dark forms of the Tagalog
zealots of independence were
squatted around the enclosure,
hugging the shadows, so that
only the lights of their cigarettes
revealed their gleaming dark
eyes. Such remarks as "Ameri-
canists," "White skinned mon-
key," "Cowardly Yancos!" pass-
ed freely in the jargon of mutter-
ings. "They would make us
slaves," and "The Yancos must
be exterminated. Mabini has said
it," and the like, were phrases
caught. In the middle of the
room was a large square Chinese
table, draped with a black satin
coverlet, each end embellished
with an equilateral triangle of
gold embroidery, at the point of
which were the letters "K."

On top of this table, in the
centre, was a human skull, pre-
sumably snatched from the public
vault at Paco Cemetery, where
were thrown the skeletons of
those whose "bono tax" were
unpaid. In front of the skull
were two bolos, crossed, their
handles inlaid with ivory, their
blades of razor sharpness, stained
a dull red, perhaps blood—per-
haps betel juice. Arrayed in
front of this paraphernalia of the
the order, at respectful distance,
sat in circular form twelve na-
tives, in black clothes, white
shirts, and at their sides black
derby hats. Each sat on a low
stool. The groups, with their
backs to the walls, were bare-
headed and barefooted—mostly
youths. The room was stifling hot
and almost airless. The matter
of oxygen was secondary. Sec-
recy was of paramount import-
ance.

Horror Tales To Awe New
Recruits

Such was the description of the
assemblage. One spoke after
another. A long series of orders
and resolutions was read nodded
to. Then a seemingly formal
ceremony took place. The skull
on the table was referred to as
that of a priest of Bigas, who
had been "punished" and the
memento kept as a reminder of
justice meted out to the friars.
In hushed tones reference was
made to four Katipunans who
joined the American constabulary,

秘密集会

在通多大教堂后面，在 amego 区，那里所有的本地人都因“被转化为和平派”而成为亲美人士，是该组织典型的集会地点。一名来自憎恨塔加禄族（Tagalog）的马卡贝贝省（Macabebe）的本地人，充当美国间谍，加入了该组织并于1889年获准进入议会。在这个黑洞里，在被发现和抓获的那个晚上，二十名通过血盟宣誓的卡蒂普南成员悄悄潜入。在场的是 Sandatahans 或 bolo 刀手的当地首领，一个聪明且狡猾的人，每天身穿白色鸭布制服，作为该市主要酒店的首席服务员出现，许多军官及其家属住在那里。独立的塔加禄狂热分子的黑色身影蹲伏在围栏周围，紧挨着阴影，以至于只有他们香烟的火光显露出他们闪烁的黑眼睛。“亲美派”、“白皮猴子”、“懦弱的 Yancos！”等话语在这种低声嘟囔的行话中随意流传。“他们会让我们成为奴隶”，以及“Yancos 必须被消灭。马比尼（Mabini）是这么说的”，等等，这类短语被捕捉到。房间中央有一张大的方形中式桌子，覆盖着黑色缎面桌布，两端饰有金绣等边三角形，三角形的顶点处绣有字母“K”。

在这张桌子的中央顶部，有一个人类头骨，据推测是从帕科公墓（Paco Cemetery）的公共墓穴中抢来的，那些未缴纳“人头税”的人的骨架就被扔在那里。头骨前面交叉放着两把 bolo 刀，刀柄镶嵌象牙，刀刃锋利如剃刀，染成暗红色，也许是血——也许是槟榔汁。在该组织的这套器具前，十二名本地人以尊重的距离围坐成一圈，身穿黑衣、白衬衫，身旁放着黑色圆顶硬礼帽。每个人都坐在一张矮凳上。背靠墙壁的一组人光头赤脚——大多是年轻人。房间里闷热得令人窒息，几乎空气不流通。氧气问题是次要的。保密至关重要。

用恐怖故事震慑新 recruits

这就是集会的描述。一个人接着一个人发言。宣读并点头通过了一系列长长的命令和决议。然后举行了一场看似正式的仪式。桌上的头骨被称为比加斯（Bigas）的一位牧师的头骨，他受到了“惩罚”，这件纪念品被保留下来，以提醒人们对修士实施的正义。人们低声提到四名加入美国警察队的卡蒂普南成员，他们被 Sandatahans 抓获，在夜间从床上被拖走，手脚被绑，头朝下被扔进井里活埋。提到了三名帕西格（Pasig）妇女，据说她们因泄露该组织的集会地点而被剥光衣服，被 bolo 刀砍成碎片，尸体被扔进沼泽。还提到了五名泰泰（Taytay）市民，他们充当美军向导，携带贿赂品被捕，被绿色藤条捆绑直至纤维切入肉中，被置于一个敞开的坟墓前，头部被铁棒击打，直到他们向前倒下，并被一把把泥土覆盖，陷入活埋的坟墓中。这些叙述的目的，显然都是为了给靠在墙边、最近刚加入该组织的新手留下深刻印象，所有这些叙述都是真实的事例。

KU KLUX KLAN

WHY IS ITS SECRET?

Original Documents Show The Aims And
Activities Of The Organization

Ku Klux Klan activities in Shanghai, since the publication of the article in the last issue of THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, have been carried out with feverish energy owing to the fact, as one communication states, that the objects of this organization are alleged to have been somewhat distorted in that article.

An explanation is necessary. In a communication sent to this office no accusations of distortion of the contents of the documents distributed were made. Reference was made only to the assertion in the article that the newspapers, as he admitted. If any "distortions" were made they were made in translation, as the documents, reproduced, are exactly as we received them.

In all explanations given by the unknown organizers of the movement the assertion of being a student body is denied. "Now the Order of the Three K's has no affiliation with any student body or movement, it is not political and neither is it Bolshevik. It is a movement of Chinese who like to better their country and themselves without the aid of foreign money or influence."

The statement that it is a student body is, in our opinion, justifiable. Much of the literature distributed to members and possible members is in English. It is difficult to see how much effect English-printed circulars would have among Chinese who do not understand English, and it is the vast majority of students who are the English-speaking and English-writing elements in China. Moreover, the aims of the organization coincide with the printed announcements of student bodies, and education is announced by the Klan as being one of their principal aims.

Ku Klux Klan was a student organization, or, to quote the actual words," or perhaps arising from ideas transmitted from America through returned students." In last week's article no attempt was made to give the context of the whole documents. Merely a general article was written on the Klan, built on information in our possession and the documents.

Below are given reproductions of the letters received by THE SUNDAY TIMES and produced to show readers exactly what documents are being circulated by the Klan. The initial "K," which heads the article, is a reproduction of the organization's seal affixed to a letter sent to this office. The "K" is interested with three dashes to emphasize the title of the organization which refers to itself as the "Order of The Three K's.'

Extensive reference has been made in the Chinese newspapers to the information we published. A certain "T. J." writing in the "Shanghai Journal of Commerce" on Thursday morning, explained the "real objects" of the organization, but he was guided only by translations of our article given in the Chinese

Emphasis is laid on its peaceful character for the accomplishment of aims eminently patriotic. Then why work in secret? Why not come out into the open and publicly reveal their existence? In America the leader of the Ku Klux Klan, the Imperial Wizard as he is called, is well-known. His photograph has appeared in practically every newspaper. Periodically public statements are made, and the only pretence at secrecy are the Klan meeting places and actions.

为何它是秘密的？

原始文件显示该组织的目标与活动

自上一期《上海星期日报》刊登相关文章以来，上海的三K党活动一直以狂热的能量进行着，原因正如一份来函所述，该文章据称在某种程度上歪曲了该组织的目标。

有必要作出解释。在寄至本办公室的一份来函中，并未指控我们歪曲了所分发文件的内容。信中仅提及文章中的一项断言，即正如他（指来信者）所承认的那样，报纸……如果有任何“歪曲”，那也是在翻译过程中产生的，因为所复制的文件与我们收到的完全一致。

在该运动不知名的组织者所作的所有解释中，都否认其是一个学生团体。“如今，‘三K团’与任何学生团体或运动均无关联，它不是政治性的，也不是布尔什维克式的。这是一场旨在改善国家及自身状况的中国人的运动，不借助外国的资金或影响。”

我们认为，称其为学生团体的说法是站得住脚的。分发给成员及潜在成员的大量文献均为英文。很难想象印有英文的传单会对不懂英文的中国人产生多大影响，而在中国，懂英语并能用英语写作的人群中，绝大多数是学生。此外，该组织的目标与学生团体的公开宣言相吻合，且三K党宣称教育是其主要目标之一。

三K党是一个学生组织，或者引用原话来说，“或许源于通过归国学生从美国传来的思想”。在上周的文章中，我们并未试图提供整份文件的上下文。仅仅是根据我们所掌握的信息和文件，撰写了一篇关于三K党的一般性文章。

下面刊登的是《星期日报》收到的信件复印件，旨在向读者确切展示三K党正在传播哪些文件。文章开头的字母“K”是附在寄至本办公室的一封信件上的组织印章的复制品。该“K”字饰有三道短划线，以强调该组织的名称，其自称为“三K团”。

中文报纸对我们发布的信息进行了广泛引用。周四上午，一位署名“T. J.”的人在《上海商报》上撰文，解释了该组织的“真实目标”，但他仅是依据该文章的中文译本进行的阐述。

在《上海商报》的文章中，神秘的“T. J.”声称，三K党无意模仿美国三K党的手段。文章强调其和平性质，以实现高度爱国的目标。那么，为何要秘密行事？为何不公开亮相，公开展示其存在？在美国，三K党的领袖，即所谓的“帝国巫师”，广为人知。他的照片几乎出现在每一份报纸上。定期发表公开声明，唯一假装保密的只是三K党的集会地点和行动。

CHINESE KU KLUX KLAN
IN SHANGHAI

A STUDENT MOVEMENT?

Organization Revealed In Documents
Distributed Among Natives

Has the Ku Klux Klan, that infamous American order of masked justice, come to China? That is a question affecting public safety which arises from an examination of some remarkable documents which have come into the possession of THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES. These documents, copies of which have been distributed to likely members, refer to the formation of an organization of the "Order of the Three K's," under "The Imperial Klan." The authenticity of the movement is worthy of consideration because our informant states: "There is no question but that the Chinese are, at present, ready for such a movement, and it would be a big source of anti-foreign spirit. This, I believe, is the object of the order."

Patriotism Behind It

The driving force of this new organization, judging from the documents, which include an invitation to join and a statement of the aims, is some degree of patriotism. Whether its activities will emulate those of the American order, whose acts of barbarism perpetrated under the mask of intense patriotism have earned for the organization world-wide abhorrence, remain to be seen. Yet, it cannot be denied that such a movement is possible of introduction in China, where secret societies and "paungs" have been known for centuries.

A large strata of Chinese society, that strata which produces the criminal elements, is honeycombed with secret orders. The loafers have their society; the robbers have their society. Whole towns and provinces have societies or "paungs," strange orders demanding undying loyalty to principles and ideas unknown to the foreigner. The only conclusion that can be attached to the new order is that it is purely a student body, perhaps arising from ideas transmitted from America through returned students, or built on the sensational stories of Ku Klux Klan activities which form an important part of the breakfast tidings in the newspapers. The dire penalties for infringement of Klan secrets, however, may be ignored if it is a student body.

among the great Powers of the world" is the appeal to prospective members, as stated on the membership form.

5 Klans; 10,000 Members

According to our information, five Klans have been formed—at Canton, Shanghai, Hangchow, Nanking and Hankow—all of which places are centres of student activity. In and around Shanghai it is understood that there are 10,000 members. The members are elected in this way: the name of a likely member is submitted to the principals of the order, and after his status has been carefully investigated, and his opinions and principles, as known to friends in the order, have been considered, he is invited to join the Klan. After he has been given time to consider the proposal a Klansman calls on him for his answer, and if he is agreeable his name is inscribed on the roll.

Few of the students who have participated in any of the student movements, and have imbibed the principles of student patriotic endeavour, should resist the appeal: "We are glad to have you in our ranks, and we know you can play an active part in this potential force to help our country."

"The Three K's"

The creed of the Klan is outlined in a document headed "Objects of the Three K's." The Klan believes in a Republican form of government and the maintenance of such a government constitutes their principal aim, as well as war on all forces detrimental to the maintenance of such a government. Monarchy is alien to the Klan.

The Klan supports and encourages education and supports the building of more schools so that the Chinese schools "can grow as efficiently and throughout the land." Purchase freely as the green grass grows of Chinese-made goods, patronage of shops selling Chinese-made goods, and support of Chinese industries are also among the Klan's objects.

Family Reverence

A strange spirit of family reverence runs throughout the document: "As we are banded together for mutual benefit we must protect our brothers, provide medical aid in case of sickness, give succour when in poverty or unemployment, or other difficulties, and to arrange for proper burial for the dead. Mother, wife and children are very dear to us and we must, therefore, give comfort and shelter to them and shield them from harm."

These are the facts of this new organization. Whether it will ever prove effective depends on the seriousness with which its members take up the work. One thing is certain: the organization is not likely to grow to the extent of the American Klan, nor will its history be written in so many chapters of lawlessness and mob-murder as in some of the southern States of America. One wonders, however, whether it is not one of those schemes bolstered up by politicians to have a loud and noisy following of students in the next struggle for dominance when President Tsao Kun has been shuffled out of the Presidency!

Confirms Previous Story

Six months ago a story was published in this paper announcing the formation of a Chinese Ku Klux Klan. It was stated that even the white gown and hood, the impressive vestment of this strange form of hooded justice, had been adopted, a yellow dragon replacing the scarlet cross of the American Klan. The objects were stated to be war on the many abuses gnawing the fabric of government in China, corruption, peculation, dishonesty among the politicians, "squeeze," and the struggle for power at the cost of national integrity.

The Klan documents in our possession confirm what was previously written. These are the objects of the Klan: Our country, right or wrong; Our brothers; Our family; Education; Industry. "Give us your answer as soon as possible so we may grasp you by the hand in the grip of brotherhood, and help to preserve our country as a nation

《上海星期日报》1924年6月18日

上海的中国三K党

是一场学生运动吗？

在本地人中分发的文件揭示了该组织

那个臭名昭著的美国蒙面正义组织——三K党，是否已来到中国？这是《上海星期日报》获得的一些非凡文件所引发的一个关乎公共安全的问题。这些文件已被复印并分发给可能的成员，涉及在“帝国三K党”之下组建一个名为“三K团”的组织。该运动的真实性值得考量，因为我们的线人指出：“毫无疑问，中国人目前对此类运动已做好准备，这将成为反外国情绪的一大源头。我相信，这就是该团体的目标。”

背后的爱国主义

从包括入会邀请和目标陈述在内的文件来看，这一新组织的驱动力是某种程度的爱国主义。其活动是否会效仿美国那个组织——后者以强烈的爱国主义为幌子实施野蛮行径，从而招致全世界的憎恶——仍有待观察。然而，不可否认的是，此类运动有可能被引入中国，因为在当地，秘密会社和“帮”已存在数个世纪。

中国社会的一个庞大阶层，即滋生犯罪分子的阶层，遍布着秘密组织。游手好闲者有其社团；抢劫者有其社团。整个城镇和省份都有社团或“帮”，这些奇特的组织要求成员对外国人未知的原则和理念保持至死不渝的忠诚。对于这个新组织，唯一能得出的结论是，它纯粹是一个学生团体，或许源于通过归国学生从美国传来的思想，或者是建立在报纸早餐新闻中占据重要地位的、关于三K党活动的耸人听闻的故事之上。不过，如果它是一个学生团体，那么违反三K党秘密的严厉惩罚可能会被忽略。

“在世界列强之中”是对潜在成员的呼吁，正如会员表上所述。

5个三K党分部；10,000名成员

根据我们所获信息，已成立了五个三K党分部——分别位于广州、上海、杭州、南京和汉口——这些地方都是学生活动的中心。据悉，在上海及其周边地区有10,000名成员。成员的选举方式如下：将潜在成员的姓名提交给该团体的负责人，在仔细调查其身份，并考虑其在团体内朋友所知的观点和原则后，邀请其加入三K党。给予其时间考虑该提议后，一名三K党员会登门征求其答复，如果其同意，则将其名字登记在册。

那些参与过任何学生运动并汲取了学生爱国奋斗原则的学生中，很少有人能抗拒这样的呼吁：“我们很高兴你加入我们的行列，我们知道你能在这股潜在力量中发挥积极作用，以帮助我们的国家。”

“三K”

三K党的信条在一份题为“三K之目标”的文件中概述。三K党信奉共和政体，维护此类政府构成其主要目标，同时也致力于打击所有不利于维护此类政府的势力。君主制与三K党格格不入。

三K党支持并鼓励教育，支持建设更多学校，以便中国学校“能够高效地在全国范围内发展”。像青草生长一样自由购买国货，光顾出售国货的商店，以及支持中国工业，也是三K党的目标。

家族尊崇

文件中贯穿着一种奇特的家族尊崇精神：“既然我们为了共同利益而团结在一起，我们就必须保护我们的兄弟，在生病时提供医疗援助，在贫困、失业或其他困难时给予救济，并为死者安排妥善的安葬。母亲、妻子和子女对我们来说非常珍贵，因此，我们必须给予他们慰藉和庇护，并保护他们免受伤害。”

这就是这个新组织的事实。它最终是否有效，取决于其成员对待工作的认真程度。有一点是肯定的：该组织不太可能发展到美国三K党那样的规模，其历史也不会像在美国南部某些州那样，写下那么多无法无天和暴民谋杀的篇章。然而，人们不禁怀疑，这是否是政客们扶持的方案之一，以便在曹锟总统被赶下台后的下一次权力争夺中，拥有一群大声喧哗的学生追随者！

证实此前的报道

六个月前，本报刊登了一则消息，宣布中国三K党成立。文中称，甚至连白袍和风帽——这种奇特的蒙面正义形式的令人印象深刻的服饰——也已被采用，只不过用黄龙取代了美国三K党的猩红十字。据称，其目标是打击侵蚀中国政府结构的诸多弊端，包括腐败、贪污、政客中的不诚实行为、“勒索”，以及以牺牲国家完整为代价的权力斗争。

我们掌握的三K党文件证实了此前所写的内容。以下是三K党的目标：我们的国家，无论对错；我们的兄弟；我们的家庭；教育；工业。“请尽快给我们答复，以便我们以兄弟般的情谊紧握你的手，并帮助将我们的国家作为一个民族保存下去
